In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and the continuing state of emergency, including masking and
social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via
teleconference. There will not be a physical location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in
the meeting in the following ways:

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter. Commission meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
868 8611 8788 Passcode: 388197. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in option from
a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 868 8611 8788 Passcode: 388197.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 868 8611
8788 Passcode: 388197.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JANUARY 10, 2022

  An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
  to order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Assembly Bill 361, this meeting was held
  via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Edler, Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Low, Olson

  Commissioners Absent:  Carman

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Cameron Hall, Code Compliance Officer
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Also Present:  John Bellas, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Michael Baker International
  Dan Wery, Michael Baker International
  Ashley Gregg, Veronica Tam & Associates
  John Muggridge, Fehr & Peers

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, DECEMBER 6, 2021

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF DECEMBER 6, 2021.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL SUCH
  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,
  APPROVE ITEM 6-A.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  B.  2021-22 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 6B

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210382; ADDRESS: 7 Sorrel Lane, Rolling Hills Estates,
  CA 90274; APPLICANT: Paul and Gina Pham; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination (NC-210383) for one and two-story additions to be constructed along the front,
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES
JANUARY 10, 2022
  1
   side and rear yards of a two-story residence with a detached garage. A Minor Deviation (MD-
  210384) is required to for the construction of a single-story addition to be built along the
  existing easterly building line that encroaches into a side yard (4'-8"), where that side yard
  was legally established but nonconforming (10' min required). A second Minor Deviation
  (MD-210385) is required for the reduction of the front yard by less than 10%. A Variance (V-
  210386) is required for the encroachment of the proposed porch addition into the required
  front yard which projects beyond the forwardmost building line.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
  Application No. PA-210382. This item was continued from the December 6, 2021 Planning
  Commission meeting in order to give staff and the applicant time to address issues that may have
  affected the required entitlements for the project. The applicant was able to address the issue by
  redesigning the roof line on the easterly side of the residence, and therefore no additional
  entitlements were required.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that Planning Commission, open the
  Public Hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the Public Hearing; and adopt
  Resolution No. PA-210382, approving the project.

  Paul Pham, Property Owner, provided a presentation with an overview of their project including
  family background, and involvement with their community and neighborhood. Mr. Pham stated that
  they have shared the plans with their neighbors; their neighbors provided signatures in support of
  their proposed project. Mr. Pham stated that they would like to develop a home that enhances their
  quality of life, allow them to raise their kids more practically, improve flow, and be able to host their
  neighbors and guests.

  Jeff Lyon, Architect, stated that it has been a pleasure working with Mr. Pham and stated that he is
  dedicated to maintaining the style of the home, and hopes that the Planning Commission will
  approve this project.

  CHAIR EDLER opened the public hearing.

  CHAIR EDLER closed the public hearing.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that Mr. Pham and Mr. Lyon did a great job with their
  presentation. He also thanked Mr. and Mrs. Pham for their service (Mr. Pham is a firefighter and
  Mrs. Pham is an Emergency Room Nurse).

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about feedback from the HOA. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that the Dapplegray Lane HOA provided two review letters approving the project.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there was any opposition by any of the neighbors on this project.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the neighbors were in support of this project and were
  included in one of thirty-five signatures obtained by the property owner.

  COMMISSIONER LOW stated that the applicant did a great job with the presentation. Upon driving
  by the project site, she observed that even with the addition of the front patio area, this home will
  still be setback further than several of their neighbors. COMMISSIONER LOW stated that this is a
  great project, especially for a growing family.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-210382, APPROVING THE PROJECT WITH THE
  PROPOSED MINOR DEVIATIONS AND VARIANCE AS PROPOSED BY STAFF.

  AYES: EDLER, MEDAWAR, SCACHTER, YOO, LOW, OLSON
  NOES:
  ABSENT: CARMAN
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No.
  210382. There is a 20-day appeal period for any member of the public or the City Council by their
  own motion.

  B. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 210363; Draft General Plan 2040 and Draft Final
  Environmental Impact Report (FEIR)

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that this is the second meeting for the Draft General Plan 2040.
  She introduced the consultant teams from Michael Baker International (MBI), Fehr & Peers, and
  Veronica Tam & Associates.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES
JANUARY 10, 2022
  2
   John Bellas, MBI, presented an overview of the Draft General Plan Update, and stated that the City
  has gone through the EIR process. Comments were taken on the Initial Study and they were
  addressed; a Draft EIR was prepared with the comment period ending on December 6, 2021. Three
  comment letters were received and these comments were addressed and included in the Draft Final
  EIR. If the Planning Commission moves this forward, it will go to the City Council for their approval.

  The three letters that were received were from the LA County Fire Department, LA County Sanitation
  Districts, and the Metropolitan Water District. The LA County Fire Department responds when they
  receive CEQA documents and virtually had no comments. The LA County Sanitation Districts
  provided a letter initially in response to the Initial Study and Notice of Preparation for the EIR. A
  follow-up letter was sent in response to the Draft EIR, which updated their flow calculations. The
  Metropolitan Water District wanted to clarify how the PV Reservoir was referenced in the EIR and
  the General Plan.

  Mr. Bellas stated that some of the changes included: A clarification to Section 4.3, Biological
  Resources, pg. 4.3-12, explaining why the reservoir has been classified as a lake; an update to
  Section 4.19, Utilities and Service System – Wastewater Pg 4.19-5, Change in quantities of average
  processing of Wastewater and remaining capacity. The most substantive change to the Final EIR is
  the Topical Response on evacuation in relation to Wildfire.

  Changes to the General Plan Update Document included: Conservation Element - Page 5-19:
  Explaining why the reservoir has been classified as a lake; Safety Element – Page 7-16: correction
  regarding ownership of feeder pipelines to the PV Reservoir as well as outlet piping; and
  Sustainability Element – Page 9-60: Change policy language ENG Policy 9-2-4 Promote to Prioritize.

  Mr. Bellas provided an overview of the next steps.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission, reopen
  the Public Hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues related to the Draft General Plan 2040
  and Draft FEIR; close the Public Hearing; and adopt Resolution No. PA-210363, recommending that
  the City Council certify the Rolling Hills Estates 2040 General Plan Final Environmental Impact
  Report and adopt the Rolling Hills Estates 2040 General Plan.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR thanked Mr. Bellas and the entire team for their work on the General
  Plan and stated that the end result was very positive.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. PA-210363, RECOMMENDING THAT THE CITY COUNCIL
  CERTIFY ROLLING HILLS ESTATE GENERAL PLAN 2040 AND FINAL
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT.

  AYES: EDLER, MEDAWAR, SCACHTER, YOO, LOW, OLSON
  NOES:
  ABSENT: CARMAN
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has adopted Resolution No. PA-
  210363, and it will move forward to the City Council at their next meeting of Tuesday, January 25,
  2022.

  8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210371; ADDRESS: 62 Buckskin Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Kristi Skelton, AIA, Unbound Architecture; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210426) for a 982.3 square-foot addition to
  an existing split-level, single-family residence. A Minor Deviation (MD-210372) is required
  for a single-story addition built along existing building lines that encroaches into a side yard

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES
JANUARY 10, 2022
  3
   where that side yard was legally established but is nonconforming. A second Minor Deviation
  (MD-210373) is required for the reduction of the front yard by less than 10%. A silhouette
  has been constructed on the site to demonstrate the mass and bulk of the proposed additions
  and was certified on November 19, 2021.

  Associate Planner Flores provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
  Application No. PA-210371.

  Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve PA-
  210371 subject to the conditions of approval noted in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired about the date the notices were mailed. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that the notices for this project were sent earlier than usual due to the Christmas
  and New Year Holiday.

  COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that he has known the applicant, Kristi Skelton for more than 35
  years, but has had no contact with her for the past 10 years. COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that
  he has no interest or involvement in her business and stated that he has no reason to be biased
  one way or the other on this project.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked about the unpermitted room that is being converted and asked if
  there is any concern that the room will be reconverted to a bedroom. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that this room does not have full head height, however, the new underfloor area does. Staff
  discussed the intended use with the applicant who stated that this would be used for storage. If
  things are done without permits in the future, then it would become a code enforcement issue.

  Kareena Dong, Property Owner, stated that she is hoping to provide more rooms for her growing
  children. Mrs. Dong stated that she grew up in the Dapplegray Lanes neighborhood and is excited
  to be back to raise her own family in the same community.

  Kristi Skelton, Architect, stated that the house next door is set far back and is not intruding on their
  private space in any way. It is nice for them to have all their family on one level.

  COMMISSIONER YOO inquired if there were any objections from the neighbors. Ms. Skelton stated
  that there were no objections and there were signatures provided by the immediate neighbors.

  Mrs. Dong stated that with the addition adjacent to 60 Buckskin, there will be 15-20 feet behind their
  property. On the other side, adjacent to 64 Buckskin, there will be bedrooms with modest windows,
  and they are not looking into any of their living spaces.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVAL PA-210371 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL NOTED IN THE
  STAFF REPORT.

  AYES: EDLER, MEDAWAR, SCACHTER, YOO, LOW, OLSON
  NOES:
  ABSENT: CARMAN
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. 210371. There is a 20-day appeal period for any member of the public or the City
  Council by their own motion.

  9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about power outages, which are affecting businesses in the
  Business District. Director Wahba stated that SCE informed him that the power outages had to do
  with the recent rains and stated that SCE is making upgrades in residential areas. They are also
  doing fly overs to look at poles.

  CHAIR EDLER asked about if there have been anymore developments on determining the view
  corridor and plantings along the Casaba berm. Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff was
  discussing this today and more research is needed. Staff will have more information within the next
  week.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR welcomed COMMISSIONER LOW and COMMISSIONER OLSON.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES
JANUARY 10, 2022
  4
   10.  MANAGER ITEMS

  A.  2022 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULE

  Planning Manager Naughton welcomed COMMISSIONER LOW and COMMISSIONER OLSON.
  She also introduced Dean Flores, Associate Planner.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS – DECEMBER 13, 2021

  COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR EDLER adjourned the meeting at 8:25 pm.

  Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Rick Edler, Chair
